_README: Copy this to %USERPROFILE%\.gemini\antigravity-cli\settings.json (create the
directory if the agy CLI has never run). PER MACHINE - it is not in this repo's
checkout path and does not travel with a clone.
WHY IT MATTERS. With no settings file the agy CLI starts with permissions=<nil> and
toolPermission=request-review, and headless mode auto-denies every shell command
because it cannot prompt anyone. The turn still returns status SUCCESS with an empty
response and exit code 0, so the seat looks like it had nothing to say. Verified
2026-09-15: creating this file flips the CLI's startup log from permissions=<nil> to
permissions=&{Allow:[...]}, which settles GitHub issue #548 - allow-rules ARE honoured
headless in agy 1.2.3, and that issue is stale.
RULE SYNTAX. command(x) matches by prefix, so command(git) covers git add, git log and
so on. Do NOT write unsandboxed(...) rules even though a stderr message may tell you
to: the binary states 'unsandboxed is no longer a valid rule, use command() instead'.
File reads inside a detected workspace (a git repo) are auto-allowed and need no rule;
a directory that is not a workspace is outside that grant and will be denied.
THIS FILE IS NOT THE WHOLE FIX. Two other things were needed to take a SIMPLE
tool-using headless turn from timing out at 5m30s having burned 195,056 input tokens
for an empty reply, down to 40 seconds and 27,320 tokens:
1. --new-project on the invocation. Without it the CLI resumes the project's
persisted model from conversation_summaries.db and ignores --model, which is how
a reasoning tier got selected and thought for five minutes.
2. A prompt giving exact file paths and forbidding directory search. When the find
tool hits a context deadline the agent falls back to recursive list_dir and burns
context without bound - that, not permissions, was the token burn.
Both are already in the GEMPRO seat in seats.example.jsonc.
AND IT IS STILL NOT PROVEN FOR REVIEW TURNS. The 40-second result was a trivial task
(read one named file, return a token). A real review turn through run-seat.mjs was
still in progress at a 150s print-timeout after 73,030 input tokens and produced no
section. GEMPRO is experimental; GPT via codex is the seat that works.
PATHS, in portable form. All five verified to exist on the ben machine 2026-09-15.
Write them as %USERPROFILE% and never as C:\Users\ben - the other machine in this
repo runs as bengr, so an absolute path from one machine is wrong on the other:
settings (this file)  %USERPROFILE%\.gemini\antigravity-cli\settings.json
CLI logs              %USERPROFILE%\.gemini\antigravity-cli\log\
persisted model state %USERPROFILE%\.gemini\antigravity-cli\conversation_summaries.db
IDE equivalent        %USERPROFILE%\.gemini\antigravity\conversation_summaries.db
the binary            %USERPROFILE%\AppData\Local\agy\bin\agy.exe
The CLI state directory (antigravity-cli) is SEPARATE from the IDE's (antigravity).
Looking in the IDE's for a CLI conversation finds nothing and misleads.
The log directory is the best debugging surface: it records the startup permission
state, which tool was denied, and the find_handler context deadline that precedes a
runaway list_dir. Reading it costs no model tokens.
Delete the _README key before use if you prefer; the CLI ignores unknown keys, but it
is noise in a config you will read again.
THE CLI RE-SERIALISES THIS FILE ON ITS FIRST RUN (verified agy 1.2.3 on the bengr
machine, 2026-09-15): < and & come back as \u003c and \u0026, the empty deny and ask
arrays are dropped, _README and the allow rules survive. Same meaning, different
bytes. So never byte-compare the installed copy against this template after the
first run; the proof that it loaded is the permissions= line in the startup log.
